instructions: Crack the 6 eggs into a large bowl and beat them well. Whisk in the 1 1/2 cups milk.
Whisk in the 1 cup flour a little at a time, until the batter is smooth with no lumps left.
Thinly slice 6 of the green onions. Finely chop about 1/4 cup of the parsley and about 1/4 cup of the dill. Crumble the feta. That should be about 1 1/2 cups.
Stir the green onions, parsley, dill and feta into the batter with the 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper and 3/4 tsp paprika.
Heat a nonstick frying pan over medium low and add about 1/2 tbsp of the olive oil. Pour in a ladle of batter, enough to cover the bottom, and tilt the pan so it spreads into a thin, even layer.
Cook it for about 2 minutes, until the top has set and the edges are golden. Flip it and cook the other side for about 1 minute.
Slide it onto a plate and cover it loosely with foil. Make the rest the same way, adding a little of the remaining olive oil to the pan each time. You'll get about 8.
Fold or roll each one up. Serve warm, two each, with the red pepper flakes on the side.
method_notes: None of the versions found had a rating count of 20 or more, and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for this cuisine, has no kaygana, so Cooking Gorgeous (5.0 from 2 votes) leads. All three whisk eggs with flour and milk into a thin batter full of parsley and green onion and cook it in a lightly greased pan like a thick crepe, flipping once. Cooking Gorgeous adds dill, paprika and feta and cooks slowly over medium low; Özlem Warren makes thinner crepes in butter over medium high with no cheese; Almost Turkish Recipes stirs in feta and red pepper flakes. This one follows the lead scaled up to 6 eggs so four people get two each, and moves the red pepper flakes to the table.
